candidates.summary: the gnoweb seed realms are merged into Plan.Realms with no marker, so a realm that is genuinely affected by the changed package is misread as a sample and vanishes from the comment
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request touching gnoweb (or contribs/gnodev) and examples/gno.land/p/nt/ownable/v0: `gnopreview plan` on the tree at this head returns 7 affected realms without the gnoweb file, gno.land/r/gnoland/home among them, and 10 with it. Because Plan.Realms carries no seed flag, comment.go:157 isSeed() tests membership in gnowebSeedRealms, which now matches home; comment.go:69 drops it from the "Realms affected through a changed package (N)" list and out of N. The reviewer of a PR that changes gnoweb and a widely imported package is told the site's landing page is unaffected, while the preview renders it.
candidates.verify_by: go test -run TestSeedRealmAffectedIsHiddenFromComment -v ./misc/gnopreview with the artifact copied in: a plan whose Realms are [gno.land/r/gnoland/home gno.land/r/x/other], both affected by the same changed package, and a Comment() that names only other. Cross-checked on the real tree with `gnopreview plan -root . -changed` on ownable.gno with and without gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app.go.
candidates.evidence: plan -changed 'examples/gno.land/p/nt/ownable/v0/ownable.gno' -> {"gnoweb":false,"n":7,"realms":[... "gno.land/r/gnoland/home" ...]}; adding gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app.go -> {"gnoweb":true,"n":10}. Unit repro: "**Realms affected through a changed package (1)**" listing only gno.land/r/x/other, with "BUG: the comment never names gno.land/r/gnoland/home, which the plan renders as affected by [gno.land/p/x/base/v0]" and "BUG: the comment counts 1 affected realm; the plan rendered 2" -> FAIL: TestSeedRealmAffectedIsHiddenFromComment

candidates.summary: Dirs and ChangedFiles, the two BuildPlan outputs gnodev and the crawler actually consume, are asserted by no test, and the Dirs[i]/Realms[i] pairing renderBase indexes by is pinned by nothing
candidates.failure_scenario: plan_test.go asserts Gnoweb, Realms, Mode, Dropped and Empty and never reads Dirs or ChangedFiles (grep -c 'Dirs\|ChangedFiles' misc/gnopreview/plan_test.go = 0). main.go:241 pairs them positionally, os.Stat(baseRoot + plan.Dirs[i]) for plan.Realms[i]; any later edit that appends to or reorders Realms after the Dirs loop (the seed append already sits one block above it) makes renderBase stat and boot the wrong directory, so a before/after pair shows another realm's page and the mislabel ships in the PR comment. ChangedFiles is the crawler's per-file gate (crawl.go:209 wantFile), so an empty or wrongly keyed map silently drops every source page of a changed realm, again with no test red.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'Dirs\|ChangedFiles' misc/gnopreview/plan_test.go returns nothing; then swap the seed-append block below the Dirs loop in BuildPlan and run go test ./misc/gnopreview — it stays green while renderBase pairs a realm with another realm's directory.

candidates.summary: Pkg.Path is derived from the directory while the import graph is keyed by module path, so a package whose gnomod.toml module differs from its directory drops out of the dependency graph silently
candidates.failure_scenario: dependents() keys rev by the import strings found in source, and seeds it with Pkg.Path, which LoadPkgs computes as the directory under examples/. A package declaring `module = "gno.land/p/x/y"` in examples/gno.land/p/x/y/v2 is stored as gno.land/p/x/y/v2, so nothing that imports gno.land/p/x/y is reachable from it: a change to that package previews zero realms and the PR comment reports none affected. Latent at this head — measured 0 of 145 gnomod.toml files under examples/gno.land where module differs from the directory — and fakeRepo() in plan_test.go always writes the two equal, so no test would catch the day it stops holding.
candidates.verify_by: for each examples/gno.land/**/gnomod.toml compare the module line against the directory: 145 files, 0 mismatches today. Make one mismatch in fakeRepo and BuildPlan drops the dependent.

candidates.summary: the hidden-directory guard in LoadPkgs returns nil rather than fs.SkipDir, so it skips the dotted directory entry and still walks everything under it
candidates.failure_scenario: WalkDir reads `if !d.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(d.Name(), ".") { return nil }` as continue, not prune, so a package under examples/gno.land/.something is loaded exactly as if the guard were absent; the only thing the branch achieves is skipping the dotted directory's own gnomod.toml. find examples/gno.land -type d -name '.*' returns 0 today, so the guard protects nothing either way and the intent it states is untested.
candidates.verify_by: find examples/gno.land -type d -name '.*' | wc -l -> 0; mkdir examples/gno.land/.hidden/r/x/z with a gnomod.toml and a lib.gno and LoadPkgs returns it.
